=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: After MAX_SECURITY_PASS_KEEP_FIXING_ROUNDS is exceeded, the keep-fixing cap should not allow an unbounded sequence of fix issues to be created for persistent blocking findings.
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6854-6871 (cap conversion logic) and the surrounding cycle budget in run_security_pass_inline.
  confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The LAST RUN DIFF intentionally narrows the cap to low/medium severity only, so a high/critical/unrated keep_fixing decision persists. The cross-pollination finding from openai/gpt-6-luna (CONSENSUS FINDINGS, scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6865-6872; 6955-6978) flags this as an unbounded loop driven by MAX_SECURITY_PASS_JUDGE_ROUNDS=0. Verification against the live script: the bounded budget is MAX_SECURITY_PASS_CYCLES (default 5) in run_security_pass_inline, which increments security_pass_cycle on every fix issue and terminalizes via security_pass_terminal_failure once the budget is spent, regardless of judge round count. MAX_SECURITY_PASS_JUDGE_ROUNDS only caps the number of judge consultations inside security_pass_exhaustion_judge, not the number of fix issues created. The narrow cap is therefore correct: persistent blocking findings (kept as keep_fixing) create up to 5 fix issues per project before terminal failure, which is the intended security backstop. The cross-pollination finding is a false positive.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: 6705-6708, 6865-6872, 6955-6979 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: After MAX_SECURITY_PASS_KEEP_FIXING_ROUNDS (default 2) is exceeded, low/medium keep_fixing decisions are converted to accept_with_followup advisories for convergence, but high, critical, and unrated keep_fixing decisions pass through unchanged at lines 6872-6873. Each creates a consolidated fix issue via lines 6963-6979, which cycles through the full pipeline. MAX_SECURITY_PASS_JUDGE_ROUNDS defaults to 0 (unbounded), so a persistent high-severity finding where the judge repeatedly selects keep_fixing creates unbounded fix cycles, each consuming CI, LLM credits, and poller time per iteration with no automatic terminalization.
  WHY: A real finding that the automated pipeline cannot fully fix keeps returning to the judge, which can keep granting one more fix cycle forever. Each cycle dispatches clarify plan implement review workflows at full cost. The only escape is a judge verdict of fail or an actual code fix that eliminates the finding on re-audit.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

  WHY: `MAX_SECURITY_PASS_JUDGE_ROUNDS` defaults to 0 (unbounded), so the loop can continue indefinitely for blocking findings when the budget is spent, rather than failing as `ai:security-pass-failed`.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 6865-6872 (cap conversion) and 6955-6978 (fix issue creation); interaction with MAX_SECURITY_PASS_JUDGE_ROUNDS default at line 1940 (=0, unbounded) and the round check at line 6702 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: After `MAX_SECURITY_PASS_KEEP_FIXING_ROUNDS` is exceeded, only low/medium `keep_fixing` decisions are converted to `accept_with_followup`. High, critical, or unrated findings with `keep_fixing` remain unconverted (line 6872: the jq filter `((.finding.severity // "" | ascii_downcase) == "medium" or ... == "low")` excludes high). When `fixing_count > 0` (line 6955), a new consolidated fix issue is created (line 6975). After that fix merges, `security_pass_cycle` increments (line 19304), the re-audit finds the same high finding, `completed_cycles >= MAX_SECURITY_PASS_CYCLES` stays true (line 7481), and the exhaustion judge is called again. Since `MAX_SECURITY_PASS_JUDGE_ROUNDS` defaults to `0` (unbounded, line 1940; the guard at line 6702 is skipped because `0 -gt 0` is false), there is no deterministic bound on this loop. The judge prompt instructs it to choose `fail` when a fix is not possible, but that is model judgment, not a deterministic guard. A persistent high finding that the judge keeps believing is fixable will create fix issues indefinitely.
  WHY: With default settings (`MAX_SECURITY_PASS_JUDGE_ROUNDS=0`, `MAX_SECURITY_PASS_KEEP_FIXING_ROUNDS=2`), a high-severity finding that survives every fix attempt loops: keep_fixing -> fix issue -> merge -> re-audit -> keep_fixing -> fix issue -> ... with no deterministic termination. Each iteration costs a full fix cycle (clarify -> plan -> implement -> review) and a security re-audit. The previous code converted ALL `keep_fixing` decisions (including high) to advisories, guaranteeing convergence but waiving high-severity vulnerabilities. This change fixes the security regression but removes the deterministic convergence guarantee. Setting `MAX_SECURITY_PASS_JUDGE_ROUNDS` to a positive value would bound the loop, but the default is unbounded.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 1945-1953 (comment block for MAX_SECURITY_PASS_KEEP_FIXING_ROUNDS) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The comment says "From the next round on, every keep_fixing decision is converted to accept_with_followup ... so the loop converges without a human" and "this cap keeps the project unattended." The code at lines 6865-6872 now converts only low/medium `keep_fixing` decisions. High/critical/unrated findings remain blocking and can start another fix cycle. The comment contradicts the code.
  WHY: No runtime failure, but the stale comment misleads maintainers into believing the cap guarantees convergence for all severities. The in-function comment at lines 6711-6712 was updated correctly ("The cap applies to low/medium findings only"); this top-level comment was not.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
